# FleetRing

> FleetRing places, replicates, and fails over fleets of small SQLite databases on machines you own, one database per agent, user, or task. Agents create, find, query, follow, and drop their own databases through `fleetring mcp --agent <id>` (an MCP server that sets up its own identity on a dev node) or the `fleetring` CLI, within the scopes of their token.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): what FleetRing is, how to install it, and a five-minute quickstart.
- [Agent skill](docs/agents/SKILL.md): when to create a database, naming, labels, descriptions, expiry, and SQL patterns for memory, task state, and full-text search.
- [Agent quickstart](docs/agents/quickstart.md): one command, `fleetring mcp --agent <id>`, that starts a dev node, mints the agent its own scoped identity, and serves MCP; and `fleetring agent add` for other fleets.
- [fleetring, the binary](crates/fleetringd/README.md): the daemon and its commands, contexts, scopes and tokens, dev mode, and the MCP server.
- [CLI guide](docs/cli.md): how the `fleetring` commands, flags, and output behave.
- [Lexicon](docs/lexicon.md): the words FleetRing uses, and the ones it doesn't.

## Optional

- [ADR-0041](docs/adr/0041-agent-kit-metadata-expiry-and-mcp.md): database metadata, expiry, `db show`, and the MCP server, with the reasoning.
- [Architecture decisions](docs/adr/README.md): the index of every ADR.
